CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to evaluate the response to medication adjustments for generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches, along with an assessment of lifestyle modifications and symptom management strategies.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith presents for his follow-up appointment, reporting mixed outcomes following recent medication adjustments. He indicates a slight improvement in his anxiety levels since increasing sertraline to 300 mg daily; however, he continues to experience notable fluctuations in mood. His tension-type headaches have persisted, occurring four times per week, with intensity ratings averaging 6 out of 10. He notes that ibuprofen remains a reliable option for acute relief, but he is concerned about the cumulative use and potential gastrointestinal side effects.
Mr. Smith reports marginal improvement in sleep quality, now averaging 6 to 7 hours per night, with reduced nocturnal awakenings. He has increased the trazodone dosage to 75 mg at bedtime, which he believes has contributed to better sleep onset. However, he continues to experience morning grogginess, which he attributes to both trazodone and gabapentin, now increased to 200 mg at bedtime.
Persistent fatigue remains a challenge, especially in the afternoons, with Mr. Smith expressing frustration over his limited energy levels impacting his productivity at work. He denies any new symptoms, such as chest pain, but mentions an increase in irritability and difficulty concentrating.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 300 mg daily (increased dosage) 2. Trazodone 75 mg at bedtime (increased dosage) 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime (continued) 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (continued) 6. Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly (continued) 7. Topiramate 100 mg daily (continued) 8. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (continued) 9. Gabapentin 200 mg at bedtime (increased dosage)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer, where project demands are contributing to his elevated stress levels. He has made efforts to incorporate more physical activity into his routine, reporting that he has started taking short walks during lunch breaks. His dietary habits remain consistent, with an emphasis on whole foods, and he continues to abstain from alcohol while limiting caffeine intake.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Anxiety levels moderately improved; sleep quality has slightly increased; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms. - Neurological: Increased headache frequency and intensity; no dizziness or visual disturbances reported. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue noted, particularly in the afternoons, with no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 122/78 mmHg, HR 74 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented, appears fatigued; mood appears anxious but cooperative. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed; tenderness noted in the bilateral temporal region. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears anxious with moderate distress.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 300 mg daily. Monitor for any potential side effects and assess the need for further adjustments in the next visit. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 75 mg at bedtime; evaluate the efficacy in the next follow-up. Gabapentin may be maintained at 200 mg at bedtime, with a focus on monitoring grogginess. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Recommend continuing the headache diary and consider increasing topiramate to 150 mg daily if headache frequency and intensity do not improve. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage Mr. Smith to maintain a sleep diary and consider cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) for insomnia and anxiety management. Continue to support lifestyle modifications, including regular physical activity and stress management techniques.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-11-01 to reassess symptoms, evaluate medication efficacy, and discuss any new concerns. Mr. Smith is encouraged to implement stress reduction strategies and maintain open communication regarding his treatment response.
